approval.note: Drafted by the implementing agent. Not approved. Only the user may approve or change thresholds.

scope_note: The workflow is deterministic, so exact agreement with hand-written expectations is expected. These gates check separation of duties, staleness, expiry, and audit on the reference stack with token-based reviewers; they say nothing about real identity management.

outcome_agreement.measure: cases whose outcome (approved, pending, or refused with a stable code) equals the hand-written expectation

forbidden_decision_rejection.measure: decisions by authors, requesters, feedback submitters, automated identities, non-reviewers, other tenants, and unauthorized purposes that are refused

stale_decision_rejection.measure: decisions naming the wrong content or made after the subject changed that are refused

expiry_enforcement.measure: expired reviews that refuse decisions and record exactly one expiry event

audit_completeness.measure: reviews whose events are contiguous from 1, start with the request, and carry actor and time

approvals_without_independent_review.measure: subjects reported approved without an independent approval of the exact content

subject_mutations.measure: reviewed proposals or candidates whose stored content changed

determinism.measure: reviews whose derived status is identical when re-read

protected_file_writes.measure: changes to the runtime prompt, registry contracts, goldens, thresholds, or manifest during the run

not_measured.identity_management: reviewers are reference-stack tokens with a group claim; a real identity provider and group sync are later work
not_measured.M5_gate: approving a subject is not the M5 separation_of_duties_review human gate
